  SORRIES in this family**, and it is worth the same standing as the explicit-`n` trap: `C` and `n`
  are file-level *implicit* variables, the `variable (C n)` that makes them explicit lived **inside**
  `namespace divFamZarAff` and ended with it, and `divFunctorAff` was declared after that `end` — so
  it bound them implicitly and its two `simp` lemmas could not elaborate. **A namespace boundary
  silently changes the arity of everything declared after it.** The fix is a `section Functor` with
  its own `variable (C n)`, closed before the affine-naturality section; no statement changed.
* `…AffFunctorCompare.lean`, `DivRepGlobalAffLift.lean` — the build never reached them.

well above 3300 s (an earlier attempt hit that cap rebuilding modules other lanes had invalidated,
`EXIT=124`).

**One item, and it is unchanged since ADDENDUM 5:** the **subordinate Stacks `0B8B` input** —
an affine open `W ⊇ supp d` lying inside one member of `d.cover`. I-0492 clause 2 says USE it, do
not re-derive it; mathlib has no form of `0B8B` and this tree constructs no curve but `P¹`.

**And one item that is NOT an obligation but is the lane's real exposure, stated because a green
build hides it.** Measured **before commit `1e571f4f5`**, with the substring collision against the
chart-typed `divFamZarAffineEquiv` excluded:

> `DivFamZarAff` / `divFamZarAff` / `divFunctorAff` appeared in **zero** Lean files outside the
> `Picard/DivisorFamilyAff*.lean` family.

The widened layer was an **island**. ADDENDUM 8 §8.1 diagnosed the *cause* as a missing base-change
face and fixed the face; that did not close the island, because closing it means a **consumer** is
restated on the widened functor.

**CORRECTED IN PLACE (reviewer finding `I-0674`).** The paragraph above was written 102 seconds
before this same session falsified it, and said "no consumer has been restated" as if it were
standing state. `Picard/DivRepGlobalAffLift.lean` (commit `1e571f4f5`, listed in §9.1 above) is
exactly such a file: it restates the DD-R general-test pullback as `pullGlobalAff` and proves the
`pull_comp` law at `divFamZarAff.map`. So at HEAD the honest count is **one** file outside the
family, and that hit is legitimate rather than a stray — which is precisely what a future audit
re-measuring the island needs told, since one unexplained hit is indistinguishable from noise.

gate. **Do not read "the widened carrier is a functor" as "the widened carrier is in use".** The
cheap check, and the one to run on any replacement type in this project: grep the new carrier's name
outside the files that define it, and exclude substring collisions before believing the count.

=== ADDENDUM 10 (1550-1600) ===
## ADDENDUM 10 (2026-07-29, run 0070 session 0014) — the widening is proved STRICT, and clause 3 is measured at the DECLARATION level (BINDING; sharpens ADDENDUM 9 §9.4 and I-0667)

Three results, in descending order of how much they change the lane's status.

### 10.1 The four modules of ADDENDUM 9 are now kernel-green, and TWO of them were WRONG

ADDENDUM 9 §9.1a recorded one module green and three "fixed but not re-checked", and `I-0675`
filed that as a live hazard. All four are now verified (`lean -o`, `EXIT=0`, zero diagnostics), and
the check was worth running because **two carried real proof errors that no sorry census, job count
or `ls-tree` readback could see**:

* `DivisorFamilyAffFunctorCompare.lean:78` — the two backward rewrites of
  `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` were placed *before* `divFamZarToAffVehicle_val`, so on the
  right-hand side there was no `_.toAff` spelling for them to match. The reported symptom was
  *"the target expression is not type-correct under the `instances` transparency level"*, which
  reads like a broken goal and is nothing of the kind — the fix is to let the forward rewrite
  normalise the spelling first.
* `DivRepGlobalAffLift.lean:145` — after the transport, `pullGlobalAff_comp`'s two sides were equal
  only up to unfolding the folded name `pullGlobalAff`; `rw`'s terminal `rfl` runs at reducible
  transparency and cannot see a plain `def`. One explicit `rfl`.

Also removed there: a redundant `[IsAffineHom pi]` binder that `[IsFinite pi]` already implies,
which had every declaration in the file emitting an overlapping-instance warning.

**Method note, and it matters under lane contention.** The check used `lean -o` writing into a
scratch olean tree seeded by *symlinks* to the project's `.lake` oleans. That writes no shared
build state, so it needs **no lake mutex** (protocol §5b) and cost ~18 s per module against a
queued `lake build` that had previously burned 3300 s and timed out.

### 10.2 THE PAYOFF IS NOW A THEOREM: the widening is strict

Everything the lane had built established that the widened carrier is *well-formed and usable*.
Nothing established that it **buys** anything. The claim that it does appeared only as prose —
`DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean:249` says "the converse is FALSE, and that failure is the content of
R2" — while both of its halves had been landed theorems for days. `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStrict.lean`
composes them:

    isCertified_affine_and_not_isCertified_chart
      -- at ONE divisor, ONE degree, ONE base:
      --   (∃ widened cover + adaptation) certified at n
      --   ∧ ∀ chart-typed adaptation, ∀ degree, NOT certified

This is the R2 justification in the form a reviewer can check. Per `reduction-needs-its-converse`,
`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` was a `≤` and a `≤` is only a *strict* widening once
something is exhibited on the far side; this exhibits it. **No hypothesis on `|P¹(k)|` occurs in
either half** — which is the field-uniformity R2 was chosen for over a field-size hypothesis.

**Scope, and it is stated in the file rather than only here.** The separation is CONDITIONAL and is
**not** certified non-vacuous. The witness exists mathematically over every field including `F₂`
(§4.3), but formalising it is out of scope by §4.5 — it needs `Sym^g C` with its universal flat
divisor. Critically, the lane's existing `n = 0` non-vacuity witnesses **do not** inhabit these

=== spec:1505-1515 ===

The proof needs no gluing: the componentwise image of the chart-typed glued value already has the
*widened* pullback property, because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the
chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the corresponding widened clause, and widened uniqueness
(`divFamZarAff.mapVal_eq_of`) closes it.

Direction: **old → new only**, and that is content, not omission. By ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4
§4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can
confine, so no transformation back can exist.

### 9.4 What the R2 lane owes after this

=== FunctorCompare.lean:28-42 ===
because `DivFamZar.toAff_mapAlgHom` turns each clause of the chart-typed `mapVal_spec` into the
corresponding widened clause.  No gluing is redone.

## The direction, and it is not an omission

Old → new only.  A widened certificate cover is an arbitrary family of affine opens, and by
`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 / ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 there is a straddling divisor at every
genus `≥ 2` that no fixed pair of `P¹` charts can confine — so no natural transformation back can
exist.  That failure is the content of R2 (protection I-0492), not a gap in this file.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFamZarToAffVehicle_map` — the comparison commutes with restriction along
  an arbitrary morphism of test objects.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctorToAff` — the natural transformation `divFunctor ⟶ divFunctorAff`.

=== DivRepGlobalAffLift.lean:30-45 ===
DD-R stack, not merely well-formed.  A functor nothing consumes and a functor everything can
consume look identical to a sorry census and to a job count.

## Direction, once more

Old → new.  A consumer that already produces a chart-typed section gets its widened counterpart
for free.  The converse does not exist and cannot: by `informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 3 §2 /
ADDENDUM 4 §4.3 a straddling divisor at genus `≥ 2` is confined by no fixed pair of `P¹` charts.
So this file does **not** claim the widened functor is representable by `DivOver`; it claims the
chart-typed representability datum pushes forward to a compatible family of widened values.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivRepAffinePullback.pullGlobalAff` — the widened general-test pullback.
* `…pullGlobalAff_val` — its value at an affine open, `toAff` of the chart-typed one.
* `…pullGlobalAff_comp` — the `pull_comp` law at `divFamZarAff.map`.
